newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI B SHARES RISE 2.8 PCT ON FOREIGN BUYING.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI B SHARES RISE 2.8 PCT ON FOREIGN BUYING.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares bounced back from morning losses to close up almost 2.8 percent on Wednesday, boosted by foreign buying, brokers said.
Losses in Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co continued on Wednesday but bargain hunting of the stock repaired damaged sentiment, helping to lift the index, they said.
The B index rose 1.969 points or 2.76 percent to 73.269 on relatively heavy turnover of $15.267 million, compared with $6.212 million on Tuesday.

Selling of Lujiazui had caused the broader market to fall on both Monday and Tuesday after the property developer on Friday announced a 67 percent year-on-year fall in 1997 interim net profit to 179.376 million yuan.
Lujiazui ended the day down $0.018 or 1.68 percent to $1.052 but buying returned after the stock touched an intraday low of $0.964, brokers said.
Buying of Eastern Communications Co, which on Tuesday reported a decent rise in 1997 interim profit, also pushed the B index higher, they said.
Eastern Communications announced net profit for the first half of 1997 was 193.227 million yuan, compared with 170.792 million yuan for the same period in 1996.
"The most important reasons (for the market's rise) were Lujiazui and Eastern Communications," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai.
"Foreign investors bought Eastern Communications and Lujiazui rebounded, so the market rose," he said.
Brokers said soaring prices of H shares, shares of Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong, have caused some foreign institutions to turn back to Shanghai B shares in rotational buying.
"There's been some positive spillover from H shares," said an analyst at another foreign securities firm in Shanghai.
Of 47 B shares, 46 shares traded with 32 up, nine flat and five down.
Eastern Communications was the top gainer on Wednesday despite a morning suspension for the results announcement. The stock rose $0.130 or 9.35 percent to $1.520.
Lujiazui was the most actively traded share on volume of around 6.8 million shares.
Brokers said the B share index could rise further on Thursday but investors would continue to keep an eye on further interim results before the end-August deadline.

Shanghai A shares continued to fall on poor sentiment but the downside would be limited after recent sharp losses, brokers said. The A index slumped 29.545 points or 2.46 percent to 1,170.608 on turnover of 3.083 billion yuan from 3.820 billion on Tuesday.
The SSE30 blue chip closed down 87.703 points or 2.44 percent to 3,501.849 points.
